findings.text: The `qoder` row launches `qoder <directive>` with no `--print`/`-p`, although the cited CLI reference says "To enter Headless mode, add the --print flag (short form -p)"; the default verdict launch opens the interactive UI instead of a headless one-shot, so it never produces the required fresh review.json.

The `qodercn` row omits the `--print`/`-p` flag that the cited Qoder CN reference requires to enter headless mode; a default `verdict run --agent qodercn` launches an interactive session and cannot deliver the review artifact.

The `neovate` row omits `-q`/`--quiet`, which the cited parser describes as the switch from interactive-by-default to non-interactive mode; the shipped default invocation stays interactive and hangs on the watchdog instead of writing a review.

The `kode` row has no `-p`/`--print` even though the cited parser defines it as "Print response and exit (useful for pipes)"; the row's positional prompt alone leaves the agent interactive, breaking the one-shot launch contract.

Spec item "Record the probe in `launcher.json`: `probe: {args, ok}`" is violated under `--rounds N`: `invoke` sets `args.probe` but this branch enters `repairLoop`, whose launcher literal never copies `args.probe`, so a multi-round launch of a clashing binary records no probe receipt.
